page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3990.17, and the uncached memory bandwidth read-only large block test reached 37.14 GB/sec. For database workloads, the Passmark database operations score is 2890.86, while Redis SET operations achieved 5.71 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds on a 7B model are limited, processing 31.57 tokens per second for prompts and 4.5 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ds_v6 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of a local 472 GB NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage without requiring external disk attachments. This hardware profile is appropriate for relational databases, caching layers, text processing applications, and moderate web serving. It is less suited for highly parallelized compilation tasks or large-scale LLM inference due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks.
